relevance_note: Family report of six BD patients over four generations; 'the heterozygous C243Y mutation was present in all familial patients with BD examined' (patients 1-5; patient 6 not sequenced).
method_note: Read the full paper; JSON assembled by a short Python script from hand-written values, every span checked verbatim by script. No tables in the paper. Labels follow the paper's most frequent form: 'patient 1', 'patient 2', 'patient 6' (lower case most often) and 'Patient 3', 'Patient 4', 'Patient 5' (only capitalised form printed). The healthy younger brother (tested negative for C243Y; also called 'her son with neither BD symptoms nor A20/TNFAIP3 mutation') is labelled 'younger brother of patient 1'; he has no variant row. Patient 6 (great-grandmother, deceased) was not sequenced ('Sequence analysis was not possible on patient 6'), so she has no variant row; the abstract's 'all affected family members carried a heterozygous C243Y mutation' contradicts this and was not used for her. Contradiction/ambiguity: Patient 6 is said to have 'recurrent oral and genital ulcers', but the next sentence says 'A history of genital ulcers could not be ascertained.' (subject unclear); her genital ulcers phenotypic_features row is kept as observed but the checklist item is 'not reported'. Variant fields for patients 2-5 (zygosity heterozygous) come from the named-group statement 'the heterozygous C243Y mutation was present in all familial patients with BD examined'; variant type 'missense' and cDNA '728 G>A' (printed without 'c.') and genomic 'chr6_138197226_G>A' are statements about this exact variant (C243Y); no transcript printed; reads were aligned to GRCh37 but the build is not attached to the coordinate, so not recorded. Patient 1 inheritance recorded 'inherited maternal' because his mother (patient 2) was sequenced and is among 'all familial patients with BD examined' carrying C243Y. Grandmother (Patient 3) is not stated to be maternal, so no inheritance recorded for patient 2 or others. Patient 1 also carries 'three nucleotide deletions in an intron of upper exon 3' (A20/TNFAIP3), recorded as its own variant row with no HGVS; not found in the mother, 'paternally derived (not investigated)', so inheritance 'not reported'. Elevated CRP for patient 1 recorded observed from 'C reactive protein 0.27 mg/dL (normal <0.1 mg/dL)' (value above printed normal; the paper does not use the word elevated). Patient 1's perianal ulcerative lesion was not counted as gastrointestinal ulcer/inflammation in the checklist. 'None of the patients had exhibited ocular lesions of BD' was applied to patients 1-6 as a named-group exclusion (ocular lesions -> uveitis or other ocular inflammation excluded). The brother's 'neither BD symptoms' was recorded as one excluded feature and not spread to checklist items. n_patients_reported left null: authors state '6 patients over 4 generations' (cohort_size_as_stated=6) but only five were sequenced. Disease label 'BD' for Patients 3, 5 and 6 comes from 'six patients with BD have existed over four generations'.

functional_evidence_statement.value: mononuclear cells from patient 1 produced large amounts of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α on LPS compared with normal controls; C243Y A20 transfected THP-1 cells suppressed IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α secretion much less than wild-type A20; impaired suppression of Nod2-mediated NF-κB activation in HEK293T luciferase reporter assay; authors regard it as a weak-function, not complete loss-of-function, variant
span: the mononuclear cells obtained from patient 1 produced large amounts of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α on LPS at various concentrations as compared with normal controls
Although inflammatory cytokine secretion was suppressed by wild-type transfected cells, it was suppressed to a much lesser extent by mutated C243Y A20/TNFAIP3-transfected cells.
In addition, impaired suppression of Nod2-mediated NF-κB activation by C243Y A20/TNFAIP3 was observed.
This finding indicates that the A20 variant possessing the C243Y mutation should be regarded as a variant that does not cause complete loss of function, but, rather, causes weak function.
